prerequisites: Fractions and reciprocals with explicit units.
explanation: Choose one whole job or a convenient number of equal work units. Keep that same whole for completed and remaining work.

worked.action: Treat painting one complete room as one job.
worked.justification: A job is a chosen whole, not a time unit.

worked.action: Equivalently call that job 60 work units; painting 15 units completes 15/60 =1/4 job.
worked.justification: Changing the scale does not change the fraction completed.

worked.action: The remaining work is 1-1/4 =3/4 job, or 45 work units.
worked.justification: Completed and remaining work must sum to the same chosen whole.

hint: Choose work units and label each rate with work/time before calculating.
shortcut: Use work = rate times active time; a convenient common work unit can avoid awkward fractions.
limitation: The rates must describe the same job, remain constant during each modelled interval, and not interfere.

entry.stem: A complete wall-painting job is defined as 24 equal work units. 6 units are complete. What fraction of the job is complete?
explanations: A unit count alone is not a fraction of the whole.
The total counts all work, not completed fraction.
repairs: Completed / whole =1/4. Label work, rate and elapsed time separately, then reconstruct the equation.
3/4 is remaining work. Label work, rate and elapsed time separately, then reconstruct the equation.
A unit count alone is not a fraction of the whole. Label work, rate and elapsed time separately, then reconstruct the equation.
The total counts all work, not completed fraction. Label work, rate and elapsed time separately, then reconstruct the equation.
